title: LLM-as-a-Demographic: Whom Sociodemographic Prompting Helps, and Whom It Hurts

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) between LLM predicted label distributions on subjective tasks and human label distributions from different racial groups (Asian, Black, White) under unconditioned and persona-conditioned prompting.
Evaluating the alignment of LLM predicted label distributions against the judgment distributions of male and female annotators under unconditioned and gender-conditioned prompting.
Measuring how closely LLM judgment distributions match human annotator judgment distributions across various age brackets (from 18-24 to 60-69) with and without age-specific demographic profiles.

Scoring LLM predictions against the label distributions of annotators with different educational attainment levels (High school or below, College degree, Graduate degree) to test default alignment and steerability.

Testing two-attribute demographic combinations (e.g., gender and race, such as 'Woman' and 'Black') in prompts to evaluate whether intersectional profiles amplify or mitigate alignment compared to the corresponding human intersectional groups.
